title: The Missing Letter
premise: Sebastian Joubert, the unassuming archivist of Saint-Aubin Cathedral, has spent years cataloguing the dead while quietly proving that three 'accidental' deaths were murders no one wanted to investigate. When a drowned stranger washes up wearing clothes stolen from Sebastian's own locked closet—clothes only one living person could have taken—the police finally look at the archivist himself. The trail leads to Marguerite Vasseur, a witness to the original crime whom every record insists is dead, and whose survival threatens both the cathedral's powerful patrons and the quiet love growing between her and Sebastian. As the tide recedes from the mudflats where the truth was buried, Sebastian must choose between the institution that gave him sanctuary and the woman it erased. In the end, he exposes the canon who ordered the killings, and Marguerite—alive, documented, and free—walks out of the crypt's shadow into a life neither of them dared plan.
about_author: Lior Reyes is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade among ledgers, seals, and things best left uncatalogued. They write mysteries about people history tried to file away.

chapters.title: The Catalogue of Small Deaths
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. In the cathedral archive, Sebastian finishes a private dossier proving three 'accidents' were murders, then locks it away as they always do. The beat is controlled loneliness: justice kept in a drawer, invisible by design.

chapters.title: Clothes That Fit a Ghost
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A drowned body is pulled from the harbor wearing Sebastian's own stolen coat and scarf, items kept in a closet only Sebastian enters. Shock curdles into fear: someone is staging Sebastian as victim or suspect.

chapters.title: Inspector Brannigan's Patience
chapters.summary: Brannigan's POV. The inspector who once dismissed Sebastian's letters now interrogates them with new, uncomfortable attention. He reveals the coat was taken months ago. Beat: the hunter realizing the mouse has been watching him back.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Forgot
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Searching burial registers, Sebastian finds a page razored out—dated the night of the first death—and a marginal note in a hand they almost recognize. Beat: dread mixed with the thrill of being needed again.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Confessional
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A veiled woman leaves a note in the confessional: 'You wore my name for eleven years.' She warns Sebastian to stop digging, but her handwriting matches the ledger note. Beat: terror braided with longing.

chapters.title: Marguerite Vasseur, Deceased
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Records show Marguerite died in 2013; yet the confessional woman knew details only the true witness could know. Sebastian realizes the dead woman in the harbor may be the body that made Marguerite 'dead.' Beat: vertigo of unraveling identity.

chapters.title: The Canon's Generosity
chapters.summary: Canon Aubry's POV. The cathedral's patron offers Sebastian a promotion and a quiet transfer abroad—a gift shaped exactly like exile. His charm has teeth. Beat: power smiling while it tightens its grip.

chapters.title: Tide Tables
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Working the harbor tides against the three deaths, Sebastian finds each body surfaced on an ebb after a spring tide—the sea has been returning what was sunk. Beat: cold clarity; the pattern was always there.

chapters.title: A Room Above the Chandlery
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite, alive under a false name, watches Sebastian from her hiding place and debates whether using him will save or destroy him. Flashback to the night she saw the first murder. Beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Fourth Accident
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A near-fatal fall in the crypt stairwell—sabotaged—tells Sebastian the canon knows how close they are. Bruised and furious, Sebastian stops hiding the dossier. Beat: invisibility abandoned; the archivist becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Coat
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Sebastian meet at last in the bell tower. She admits she stole his clothes years ago as insurance—proof she could vanish into him if ever cornered. Someone found her cache. Beat: wary tenderness between two people built of aliases.

chapters.title: The Drowned Man's Hands
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The harbor victim's calloused hands identify him as a stonemason who worked the crypt restoration—the man whose death certificate bears Marguerite's married name. Beat: grief for a stranger who died so a lie could live.

chapters.title: Brannigan's Bargain
chapters.summary: Brannigan's POV. The inspector privately concedes Sebastian was right all along, but city pressure forbids touching the canon. He offers unofficial help if Sebastian can produce proof. Beat: reluctant alliance, duty bending toward conscience.

chapters.title: The Crypt Beneath the Crypt
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Behind a sealed ossuary wall, Sebastian finds a hidden chamber: financial records showing the canon laundering money through restoration contracts, and a fresh grave dug and refilled. Beat: awe turning to horror at what holiness buried.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Mud
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite confesses everything: she witnessed the mason's murder, was declared dead to silence her, and has lived off borrowed names since. She asks Sebastian to let the tide keep its secret. Beat: love against duty, stated plainly at last.

chapters.title: The Letter That Started It
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Among the hidden papers is the original letter Marguerite wrote naming the killer—the 'missing letter' the canon has hunted for a decade, which Sebastian unknowingly catalogued years ago. Beat: the archive itself becomes the weapon.

chapters.title: Vespers for a Trap
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Sebastian lets slip the letter's location, knowing the canon must come for it during evening service. Brannigan waits in the shadows; Marguerite refuses to stay hidden. Beat: coiled anticipation before the strike.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gave Up
chapters.summary: Climax begins. The canon confronts Sebastian in the crypt, and Marguerite steps out of the dark—alive, which unravels his entire architecture of lies. Violence flares; the tide-driven flooding of the lower crypt becomes the battlefield. Beat: terror and defiance.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Climax resolves. Brannigan arrives as the rising water traps them; the canon, fleeing through the flooded passage he once used to dispose of bodies, drowns in the same ebb channel. Sebastian saves Marguerite, nearly drowning themselves. Beat: catharsis paid in salt and fear.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite gives her statement—her real name spoken aloud for the first time in eleven years—as the legally dead witness resurrected on paper. Brannigan reopens all four cases. Beat: trembling relief; identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: Recataloguing
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian files the true account of all four deaths into the permanent record, correcting the ledger page that was cut out, and resigns the anonymity that once protected them. Beat: quiet triumph; the archivist chooses to be seen.

chapters.title: Low Tide, Morning
chapters.summary: Shared final scene. On the mudflats at low tide, Sebastian and Marguerite walk where the sea gave up its dead, planning a life with no false names in it. The last line belongs to the tide going out. Beat: earned peace, love chosen over duty's shadow.
